introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0510 Biology 1, June 2022, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section I (questions 1-7): independent questions. Section II (questions 8-20): biological diagrams. Section III (questions 21-25): one or more responses correct. Section IV (questions 26-30): pairs of statements. Section V (questions 31-40): lettered headings and a description. Section VI (questions 41-50): biological situations.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION I - directions as printed, summarised:* Each of these questions or incomplete statements is followed by four suggested answers. Select the best answer in each case and mark the answer sheet appropriately.

Which group of bacteria would cause a decrease in soil fertility?
questions.corrige_markdown: Denitrifying bacteria convert nitrates in the soil into nitrogen gas, which escapes to the atmosphere. The soil therefore loses the nitrate that plants need, so its fertility falls. Saprophytic bacteria decompose dead matter and release nutrients, nitrogen fixing bacteria add nitrogen compounds, and nitrifying bacteria change ammonia to nitrates: all three increase or maintain fertility. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: It is one of the reasons for the success of insects in nature.
questions.corrige_markdown: Insects are successful because most can fly, so they find food and mates and colonise distant habitats quickly (other reasons: small size, waterproof exoskeleton, high reproductive rate). Insects have an exoskeleton, not an endoskeleton (B is wrong); they have compound eyes as well as simple eyes (C is wrong); and sexual reproduction is shared by most animals, so it is not a special reason for their success (D). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: They have wings that enable them reach out to distant environments.
They have an endoskeleton that protects their inner structure.
They have only simple eyes which are well adapted for vision.

questions.enonce_markdown: A normal skinned man who is married to a normal skinned woman finds out that their last baby boy is an albino. What are the probable genotypes of the couple?
questions.corrige_markdown: Albinism is recessive (aa). The child is aa, so he received one a allele from each parent. Both parents have normal skin, so each must carry the dominant allele A as well: both are Aa (carriers). Cross Aa x Aa gives AA : Aa : Aa : aa, so a 1 in 4 chance of an albino child. Aa and aa (A) would give an albino parent; AA and aa (B) and Aa and AA (C) can never produce an aa child. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below shows the carbon cycle.

![fig-1](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

Which of the following processes are represented by the letters P, W and R?

| | P | W | R |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Respiration | Photosynthesis | Combustion |
| B | Respiration | Combustion | Decay |
| C | Respiration | Combustion | Oxidation |
| D | Combustion | Respiration | Decay |
questions.corrige_markdown: W is the arrow from carbon dioxide in the atmosphere to carbon in plants: plants take in carbon dioxide, so W is photosynthesis. P is the arrow from carbon in animals back to the atmosphere: animals release carbon dioxide by respiration. R is the arrow from fuels back to the atmosphere: burning fuels releases carbon dioxide, so R is combustion. S (plants to animals) is feeding. Only option A has all three correct. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: P: Respiration; W: Photosynthesis; R: Combustion
P: Respiration; W: Combustion; R: Decay
P: Respiration; W: Combustion; R: Oxidation
P: Combustion; W: Respiration; R: Decay

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following organisms is a producer?
questions.corrige_markdown: A producer makes its own food by photosynthesis. Spirogyra is a green alga with chloroplasts, so it is a producer. Yeast and mushroom are fungi (saprophytes, no chlorophyll) and man is a consumer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A part of the human eye that refracts light.
questions.corrige_markdown: The cornea is the transparent front of the eye; it bends (refracts) most of the incoming light. The iris controls the size of the pupil, the pupil is only an opening, and the retina is the light-sensitive layer where the image forms. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A food sample was tested with Benedict's solution and a brick- red coloration was observed. The food sample contained;
questions.corrige_markdown: Benedict's solution, heated, turns brick-red when a reducing sugar such as glucose is present (blue, green, yellow, orange, then brick-red as the concentration rises). Starch is tested with iodine, protein with biuret reagent and fats with the ethanol emulsion test. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION II - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions relates to biological diagrams. Select the best answer for each question.

The diagram below is a food chain in which the letters W, Q, X and Y represent some organisms.

Plants -> W -> Q -> X -> Y

Extinction of organism Q will
questions.corrige_markdown: W is eaten by Q. If Q becomes extinct, W loses its predator, so the population of W increases (until its own food supply, the plants, becomes limiting). X, which fed on Q, loses its food, so X decreases, not increases (B is wrong). W cannot decrease because of Q disappearing (C is wrong), and the chain is certainly affected (A is wrong). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Have no effect on the chain.
Lead to an increase in the population of X.
Lead to a decrease in the population of W.
Lead to an increase in the population of W.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagrams below show the steps involved in testing for starch in a leaf. At which step is the leaf decolorized?

![fig-2](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In the starch test the leaf is first killed and softened by boiling in water (A and C), then boiled in alcohol (ethanol) in a water bath to dissolve the chlorophyll, which decolorizes the leaf (B), and finally iodine solution is dropped on the pale leaf (D). The decolorizing step is therefore B, "Boil in alcohol". **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which part in the diagram of the mammalian brain is responsible for balance?
questions.corrige_markdown: The cerebellum coordinates muscle movements and maintains balance and posture. The cerebrum controls thinking, memory and voluntary action, the medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat and breathing, and the midbrain relays visual and auditory reflexes. (The question refers to a diagram that is not reproduced in the printed paper; the answer does not depend on it.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the diagram of the human skin.

![fig-3](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

Which part produces melanin?
questions.corrige_markdown: Melanin, the dark pigment that protects against ultraviolet light, is made by melanocytes in the deepest layer of the epidermis, the Malpighian (germinative) layer. In the diagram the epidermis shows layers 1 (outer dead cells), 2 and 3; layer 3 is the lowest, so it is the pigment-producing layer. Structure 4 is the hair follicle (its base, the papilla). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the diagram of a bony fish.

![fig-4](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Which numbered structure functions in steering the fish?

*Options as printed:* A) 2.   B) 3.   C) 4.   D) 5.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Structure 2 is the pectoral fin, just behind the gill cover. The paired pectoral fins are used for steering (turning), braking and keeping the fish stable. Structure 3 is the anal fin and 5 the dorsal fin (both prevent rolling and keep balance); structure 4 is the caudal (tail) fin, which gives the main forward thrust. Structure 1 is the pelvic fin.

**Intended answer: A (2).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the diagram of a typical plant cell.

![fig-5](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

Which structures are not found in an animal cell?
questions.corrige_markdown: Structures 1 (cell wall) and 2 (chloroplast) are found only in plant cells. The nucleus (3) and the cell membrane (4) are found in both plant and animal cells. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which structure does fertilization take place in humans?
questions.corrige_markdown: The sperm swim up through the uterus into the oviduct (Fallopian tube), where one fuses with the egg released from the ovary. The zygote then moves down to the uterus and implants. The ovary produces eggs, the uterus holds the embryo, and the vagina receives the semen. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The pancreatic juice enters the alimentary canal at the
questions.corrige_markdown: The pancreatic duct joins the bile duct and opens into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine, where the pancreatic enzymes (amylase, trypsin, lipase) act. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is that of a neurone.

![fig-6](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

Which numbered structure is the dendron?

*Options as printed:* A) 1.   B) 2.   C) 3.   D) 4.
questions.corrige_markdown: Left open because the scanned diagram does not make the answer certain. Label 1 has a short leader that stops beside the fine branching ends on the left of the cell body; label 2 points to the nucleus; label 3 points to the cell body edge; label 4 points to the myelin sheath on the axon. By elimination the dendron (the branching process of the cell body that carries impulses towards it) is the structure labelled **1**, so the most probable intended key is **A**, but the leader of label 1 does not clearly touch a structure.

questions.enonce_markdown: In the kidney, ultra-filtration takes place at the
questions.corrige_markdown: Ultrafiltration happens in the glomerulus, the knot of capillaries inside the Bowman's capsule: high blood pressure forces water, glucose, urea and salts out of the blood, while blood cells and large proteins stay behind. The proximal tubule reabsorbs glucose, the loop of Henle concentrates the filtrate and the distal tubule adjusts salts and water. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below shows a seedling.

![fig-7](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)

Select the correct option that suits the plant

| | Type of germination | Plant type |
|---|---|---|
| A | Epigeal | Monocot |
| B | Epigeal | Dicot |
| C | Hypogeal | Dicot |
| D | Hypogeal | Monocot |
questions.corrige_markdown: The two cotyledons are carried above the soil level, so germination is epigeal (hypogeal means the cotyledons stay underground). The seedling has two cotyledons, broad leaves with net (branching) veins and a branching tap root system, which are features of a dicotyledonous plant. Monocots have one cotyledon, parallel veins and fibrous roots. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Where does gaseous exchange occur in the lungs?
questions.corrige_markdown: Gaseous exchange occurs by diffusion across the thin, moist walls of the alveoli, which are surrounded by blood capillaries. The bronchi and bronchioles only carry air, and the pulmonary artery carries blood to the lungs. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A leaf is attached to the stem of a plant at the;
questions.corrige_markdown: A node is the point on the stem where a leaf (and its axillary bud) is attached; the internode is the part of the stem between two nodes. The axil is the angle between the leaf stalk and the stem, where the axillary bud grows. **Answer: B.**

Spirogyra is

1. Autotrophic.
2. Unicellular.
3. Terrestrial.
questions.corrige_markdown: Spirogyra is a green alga with spiral chloroplasts: it makes its own food by photosynthesis, so it is autotrophic (1 is correct). It is a filament of many cells, so it is multicellular and not unicellular (2 is wrong). It lives in fresh water such as ponds and slow streams, so it is aquatic and not terrestrial (3 is wrong). Only 1 is correct. **Answer: D.**

Tendons

1. Are muscular.
2. Connect muscles to bones.
3. Are tough.
questions.corrige_markdown: Tendons are made of white fibrous connective tissue: they are tough and inelastic (3) and they join muscles to bones (2). They are not muscular (1 is wrong); ligaments join bone to bone. Only 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: C.**

*SECTION III - directions as printed, summarised:* For each of the questions below, ONE or MORE of the responses is (are) correct. Decide which of the responses is (are) correct. Then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

Enzyme(s) involved in the formation of recombinant DNA.

1. Enterokinase.
2. Ligase.
3. Restriction endonuclease.
questions.corrige_markdown: Restriction endonuclease cuts the plasmid and the donor DNA at specific sites (3), and DNA ligase joins the cut ends together to form recombinant DNA (2). Enterokinase is a digestive enzyme that activates trypsinogen in the small intestine and has nothing to do with genetic engineering (1 is wrong). Only 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: C.**

Then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

Biological method(s) of controlling pests:

| 1 | Introduction of tilapia fish into a lake to eat mosquito larvae. |
|---|---|
| 2 | Use of herbicides. |
| 3 | Spraying oil on ponds to kill aquatic organisms. |
questions.corrige_markdown: Biological control uses a living organism (a predator, parasite or pathogen) to reduce a pest. Tilapia eat mosquito larvae, so 1 is biological control. Herbicides (2) and oil sprayed on ponds (3) are chemical methods. Only 1 is correct. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION III - directions as printed, summarised:* For each of the questions below, ONE or MORE of the responses is (are) correct. Decide which of the responses is (are) correct. Then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

Eutrophication involves

| 1 | The introduction of organic matter into a water body. |
|---|---|
| 2 | Death of submerged plants. |
| 3 | The overgrowth of algae in the water body. |
questions.corrige_markdown: Eutrophication starts when nutrients and organic matter (fertilisers, sewage, animal waste) enter a water body (1). The nutrients cause a rapid overgrowth of algae, an algal bloom (3). The bloom blocks light, so submerged plants die (2); bacteria decomposing the dead matter use up the dissolved oxygen and animals such as fish die. All three statements describe the process, so 1, 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: A.**

*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether the first statement is true or false and whether the second statement is true or false. Choose: A if both are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true and the second false; D if the first is false and the second true.

**First statement:** Upper epidermal cells of leaves do not contain chlorophyll.

**Second statement:** Guard cells are the only epidermal cells that contain chlorophyll.

*Options as printed:* A) True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.   B) True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.   C) True, False.   D) False, True.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true: the upper epidermis is a transparent protective layer whose cells have no chloroplasts, and the guard cells are the only epidermal cells with chloroplasts. The second statement states an exception rather than giving the reason why the other epidermal cells lack chlorophyll (they are transparent so that light reaches the palisade cells below), so the usual reading is that it is NOT a correct explanation of the first. Because a marker could also accept it as a contrast that explains the first, the question is left open for self-assessment. Most probable intended key: **B** (both true, second not an explanation).

*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether the first statement is true or false and whether the second statement is true or false. **First statement:** Oxygen is an excretory product of plants.

**Second statement:** Oxygen is produced during photosynthesis.

*Options as printed:* A) True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.   B) True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.   C) True, False.   D) False, True.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true in the school syllabus: during photosynthesis plants make oxygen, which is a waste product of the process and leaves through the stomata, so oxygen is described as an excretory product of plants, and the second statement explains why. However, many teachers do not call oxygen an excretory product, so the key is debatable and the question is left open for self-assessment. Most probable intended key: **A** (both true, and the second explains the first).

*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether the first statement is true or false and whether the second statement is true or false. **First statement:** Germinating maize seeds contain reducing sugar.

**Second statement:** Food reserves in germinating maize seed are hydrolyzed by enzymes.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both are true and linked. During germination amylase hydrolyses the starch stored in the endosperm into maltose and glucose, which are reducing sugars, so the germinating seed gives a positive Benedict's test. The second statement therefore explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether the first statement is true or false and whether the second statement is true or false. Choose: A if both are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true and the second false; D if the first is false and the second true.

**First statement:** Enzymes are protein in nature.

**Second statement:** Enzymes are denatured by high temperature.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both are true. Enzymes are made of protein, and the bonds that hold a protein in its specific shape are broken by high temperature, which changes the shape of the active site: the enzyme is denatured. So the second statement is a correct explanation of the first (being protein is the reason that heat denatures enzymes). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether the first statement is true or false and whether the second statement is true or false. Choose: A if both are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true and the second false; D if the first is false and the second true.

**First statement:** Plant cells have a fixed shape.

**Second statement:** Plant cells have no cell membrane.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: the rigid cellulose cell wall gives plant cells a fixed shape. The second is false: every plant cell has a cell membrane, just inside the cell wall. First true, second false. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION V - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of four lettered headings A, B, C, D. Select the heading which is closely related to the description which follows.

Select the heading which is closely related to the description: where sperms are stored.
questions.corrige_markdown: Sperm are made in the testes and then stored in the epididymis, the coiled tube on the surface of each testis, until ejaculation. The seminal vesicle makes the fluid of the semen and the sperm duct carries sperm to the urethra. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: transports soluble food in plants.
questions.corrige_markdown: The phloem (sieve tubes) transports dissolved food such as sucrose and amino acids from the leaves to other parts of the plant. The xylem carries water and mineral salts. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: prevents excretion of useful substances.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the kidney, useful substances such as glucose, amino acids and most of the water are taken back from the filtrate into the blood by selective reabsorption in the tubule, so they are not lost in urine. Ultrafiltration removes substances indiscriminately from the blood. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: transports soluble food to the liver.
questions.corrige_markdown: The hepatic portal vein carries blood rich in absorbed soluble food (glucose, amino acids) from the small intestine to the liver. The hepatic artery brings oxygenated blood to the liver, the hepatic vein takes blood away from it and the vena cava returns blood to the heart. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: the coloration observed when Millon's reagent is added to saliva and heated.
questions.corrige_markdown: Saliva contains the protein enzyme amylase. Millon's reagent gives a red (brick-red) precipitate or colour when heated with protein, because it reacts with the amino acid tyrosine. Blue is the colour of Benedict's solution and of the biuret reagent before it reacts. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: where starch is stored.
questions.corrige_markdown: In algae such as Spirogyra, starch made by photosynthesis is stored in the pyrenoids, the dense protein bodies in the chloroplast. The cell wall is made of cellulose, a food vacuole holds food being digested in protozoa, and the cytoplasm is the site of many chemical reactions. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: group of organisms of the same species.
questions.corrige_markdown: A population is all the individuals of one species living in the same place at the same time. A community is all the populations of different species in a habitat, and an ecosystem is the community together with its non-living environment. (Colony, such as a colony of bees, is a group living together but is not the standard ecological term.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: washing away of nutrients from top soil into the depths.
questions.corrige_markdown: Leaching is the washing down of dissolved mineral salts (nutrients) from the top soil into the deeper layers, out of reach of roots, as water drains through the soil. Erosion removes the soil itself, mainly along the surface, while flooding and drainage concern the movement of water. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: describes a potato strip after dipping in a concentrated salt solution for 30 minutes.
questions.corrige_markdown: The concentrated salt solution has a lower water potential than the cell sap, so water leaves the potato cells by osmosis. The cells lose turgor and become flaccid, and the strip becomes soft and limp (and shorter). A turgid, hard strip would be seen in distilled water. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description: a good food for an anaemic person.

*Options as printed:* A) Carrot.   B) Mango.   C) Lettuce.   D) Crayfish.
questions.corrige_markdown: Anaemia is commonly due to a lack of iron, needed to make haemoglobin, so the best food is the one richest in iron. Carrot (vitamin A) and mango (vitamin C) are not iron-rich. Lettuce is a green leafy vegetable and crayfish is a shellfish, and both can be taught as sources of iron, so the key is debatable and the question is left open for self-assessment. Most probable intended key: **D** (crayfish, an animal food whose iron is well absorbed), with **C** (lettuce) as the other defensible reading.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION VI - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions deals with biological situations. Each situation is followed by a set of questions. Select the best answer for each question.

In pea plants, the allele (R) for red flower is dominant over the allele (r) for white flower. A heterozygous red-flowered plant was crossed with a white flowered plant. The resulting offspring will be;
questions.corrige_markdown: The heterozygous red plant is Rr and the white plant is rr. Gametes: R, r from the first parent and r only from the second. Offspring: Rr (red) and rr (white) in equal numbers, so half red and half white (a 1 : 1 test cross ratio). Pink would only occur with incomplete dominance, which is not the case here. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The set up below was used in an experiment.

![fig-8](gce-ol-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)

The gas X is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Elodea (a water plant) placed in light photosynthesises and gives off bubbles of oxygen, which collect at the top of the inverted tube as gas X. It could be tested with a glowing splint, which relights. Carbon dioxide is used up, not released, in light. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Old human red blood cells lack a nucleus. This is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Mature red blood cells lose their nucleus so that there is more room for haemoglobin, and so more oxygen can be carried. Red cells do not store DNA, food or waste. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: To ensure sufficient space for oxygen transport.
To create space for DNA storage.
To ensure sufficient space for food storage.
To create space for waste storage.

questions.enonce_markdown: Water drops from leaves in the morning. This is as a result of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Guttation is the loss of liquid water (drops) through hydathodes at the leaf margins, usually at night or in the early morning when the air is humid and the stomata are closed and root pressure pushes water up. Transpiration loses water as vapour, so no drops are seen. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The contents of four blood vessels in a human were analyzed and the results were as indicated in the table below. Which of these blood vessels will likely be the pulmonary vein?

| Blood vessel | Oxygen | Glucose | Carbon dioxide |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 5 | 3 | 3 |
| B | 5 | 4 | 1 |
| C | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| D | 4 | 4 | 4 |
questions.corrige_markdown: The pulmonary vein carries blood from the lungs to the heart, so the blood has just lost carbon dioxide and gained oxygen: it has the highest oxygen content and the lowest carbon dioxide content. Vessel B (oxygen 5, carbon dioxide 1) fits. Vessel C, with low oxygen and the highest carbon dioxide, is deoxygenated blood such as in the pulmonary artery or a vein from active tissues; A has the same oxygen as B but a high carbon dioxide content, and D shows no clear difference. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Blood vessel A (oxygen 5, glucose 3, carbon dioxide 3)
Blood vessel B (oxygen 5, glucose 4, carbon dioxide 1)
Blood vessel C (oxygen 2, glucose 3, carbon dioxide 5)
Blood vessel D (oxygen 4, glucose 4, carbon dioxide 4)

questions.enonce_markdown: It is good to expose new born babies to sunlight in the morning. This is for:
questions.corrige_markdown: Ultraviolet light in sunlight acts on a fatty substance in the skin to make vitamin D, which is needed for calcium absorption and strong bones (lack causes rickets). Vitamin A comes from food, and antibodies are made by white blood cells. Melanin is made in the skin but its main role is protection, not the reason for the morning sun. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An enzyme's optimum pH is 4. Where would this enzyme work best?
questions.corrige_markdown: An optimum pH of 4 is acidic. The stomach is acidic (about pH 2 to 4 with the contents), whereas saliva in the mouth is nearly neutral (about pH 7) and the duodenum and ileum are alkaline (about pH 7.5 to 8.5). The stomach is the only acidic region, so the enzyme works best there. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: It is advisable to look into the horizon from time to time during reading. This is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: When reading, the ciliary muscles contract to make the lens thick and round to focus on near objects, which tires them. Looking at the distant horizon makes the ciliary muscles relax, the suspensory ligaments become taut and the lens becomes thin, which rests the muscles and reduces eye strain. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Give rest to rods and cones.

questions.enonce_markdown: Sperm cells are haploid. This is because sperm cells are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sperm are made by meiosis (reduction division), which halves the chromosome number from 46 to 23, so each sperm is haploid. Mitosis keeps the number unchanged (diploid cells). Where or when the sperm are produced or released does not determine their chromosome number. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In an experiment, lime water turned milky when a gas was passed through it. The gas could have been:
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water (calcium hydroxide solution) to form insoluble white calcium carbonate, which turns the solution milky. Oxygen, carbon monoxide and nitrogen dioxide do not do this. **Answer: D.**
